columns.rationale: distinct_count 3322 equals the table's row_count 3322 with null_count 0, so tailnum uniquely identifies every row and serves as the aircraft registry key.

Operator context defines year as the year manufactured; all 10 samples (1956.0-1975.0) are integral so DECIMAL(38,9) casts cleanly to INTEGER, and null_rate 0.021072 (70 nulls) means the column must stay nullable.
null_rate is 0.0 and distinct_values are exactly three categories (Fixed wing multi engine, Fixed wing single engine, Rotorcraft), so the column is complete and low-cardinality as-is.
null_rate 0.0 with 35 distinct manufacturer names (e.g. AIRBUS, BEECH, BOEING) recorded as free text from the registry; no cast is supported by the samples.
null_rate 0.0 with 127 distinct alphanumeric model codes (e.g. 172E, 210-5(205), 550) that mix letters and digits, so the column must remain text.
distinct_values are exactly 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 with null_rate 0.0, confirming an integral engine count that casts cleanly from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.
Samples (2.0, 4.0, 5.0 ... 12.0) and the min 2.0/max 450.0 range are all integral seat counts with null_rate 0.0, supporting a cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.

Operator context states speed is the average cruising speed in mph, so the unit suffix convention applies; distinct_values (90.0-432.0) are all integral supporting a cast to INTEGER, but null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows) means the column is sparsely populated and must stay nullable.

is_airbyte_metadata is true, marking this as a capture-tool identifier rather than a business column.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 3322, so no exact-duplicate removal is needed.
tailnum has distinct_count 3322 equal to row_count 3322 with null_count 0, so it uniquely identifies each aircraft record and is the only column that can serve as the declared grain.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so they are dropped.
year has null_rate 0.021072 (70 of 3322 rows), a small but real gap in registry records, so nulls are retained rather than imputed or failed.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows), making it almost entirely unpopulated, but the 13 distinct values present (90-432 mph) are retained as nullable rather than dropped.
Operator context specifies the mph unit-suffix naming convention for measures, so speed becomes speed_mph.
engine was renamed to engine_type to distinguish the 6-category engine type text column from the numeric engines count column.
year, engines, seats, and speed all land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sampled and distinct value across them is integral (e.g. engines 1.0-4.0, seats 2.0-450.0), supporting a cast to INTEGER.

purpose: This table is the cleaned FAA aircraft registry reference feeding downstream flight analyses that need per-tailnum attributes such as manufacture year, type, manufacturer, model, seating and engine configuration, and cruising speed for the aircraft observed in the 2013 NYC flights dataset.
usage: Join on tailnum to enrich flight records with aircraft attributes; consumers must handle nulls in year_manufactured and especially speed_mph, since speed_mph is populated for fewer than 1% of rows (null_rate 0.993076) and should not be assumed present without an explicit null check.
limitations: Pipeline metadata columns (_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, _airbyte_meta) were dropped entirely; speed_mph remains almost entirely null (99.3% null) and year_manufactured has a small null gap (2.1% null), neither of which could be resolved from the source data; per operator context, American Airlines and Envoy Air aircraft are absent from this registry because those carriers reported fleet numbers rather than tail numbers.
